what: A dark nebula fog drifts behind the screen — teal clouds (bright only where dense over the background) with magenta, red, green, teal and deep blue tints spread by a different noise, and an iris-like orb and rings gather at the center (form). Where the cursor passes, the fog is pushed within radius .1 and brightens (follows with 1−e^(−6·dt)), and the clouds flow upward with scroll. With shafts on, stage-light beams strike down from beyond the top of the screen. At the start it rises from the background over 2s power1.out, and fx:mood events apply inhale·swirl·rise over .8s power2.out, and in the end section red and magenta fill up. 3px scanlines roll one step every 8s (WebGL, three)

options.form: How much it gathers into the center bead and ring, 0 to 1, default 1 (home hero) — 0 on subpages
options.shafts: Light rays 0~1, default 0 (service header is 1 — original .85)
options.resolution: Drawing resolution scale, default .5 — max max(default 520000) pixels
options.fixed: If 0, not attached to the screen and laid only inside the element, default 1
options.--fx-mist-bg·tint·1~5: Background, clouds and five palette colors (CSS variables) — the defaults are the original colors derived from --kf-bg and --kf-accent (#2f9bb5 · #cc4f8c · #e4393c · #23cf48 · #17ffff · #0646ff)

use: · Final section: el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('fx:mood', { detail: { inhale: .5, swirl: .3, lift: .4, end: 1 } }))
note: The original is a cloud that ray-marches a 3D noise texture in 52 steps. This part gets the same grain with two layers of fbm. The original’s video light bleed and the glow around pictures (MistCard) are devices hung on the page, so they exist only in the site copy (shared.js). three loads three-global.js before three.cjs and receives it as window.THREE

from.where: shared.js mist() — original MistField (resolution .5, 520k pixels, speed .35, tint #2f9bb5, accent .45, five palettes, shape orb, shafts .85), subpages form 0, Service page shafts 1
